modules.title: First notes — middle C & five fingers
modules.guide:
Welcome! We'll learn the keyboard in small, friendly steps.

Sit so middle C (near the center of the piano) is in front of you. Finger numbers: thumb = 1, pinky = 5.

Pick an exercise → listen with ▶ → press I'm ready → play when each note hits the line.

lessons.title: Welcome — how Academy practice works
lessons.guide:
Each lesson works like this:

1. Read the tip in the sidebar (and the box on the notes area).
2. Press ▶ beside the exercise to hear it.
3. Press I'm ready, then ▶ in the center to play.

Learn mode waits for you — no rush. Connect a MIDI keyboard in Settings for the best experience.

lessons.title: Find middle C (right hand)
lessons.guide: Find middle C and tap it four times with your right thumb (finger 1). Think: steady, light, confident — like knocking on a door.

tourSteps.text: Look at the keyboard. Middle C sits just to the left of the group of two black keys. It's your home base on the piano.
Place your right thumb on middle C. Curve your fingers gently — like you're holding a small orange.
Four middle-C notes will fall. Press when each one touches the line at the bottom.
Not sure yet? Press ▶ beside the exercise to hear it first. Then I'm ready when you want to play yourself.

lessons.title: Five-finger walk C–G (right hand)
lessons.guide: Keep your hand on five keys: C–D–E–F–G. Walk up the ladder, then walk back down. Same keys — no reaching!

tourSteps.text: Right-hand home position: thumb (1) on C, then each finger on the next white key up to G.
Walk up: C → D → E → F → G. Lift one finger at a time — like climbing a tiny ladder.
Now walk back down: G → F → E → D → C. Same fingers, coming home.
Numbers on the falling notes show which finger to use. I'm ready → center ▶ to start!

lessons.title: Quarter-note pulses on C
lessons.guide: Four steady taps on middle C. Count 1–2–3–4 out loud — your thumb stays on the key between taps.

tourSteps.text: Count with the notes: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4. Keep the beat steady — not faster, not slower.
Thumb stays on C. Tap down on each number and lift quickly — short, bouncy notes.
Hear it once with ▶, then try matching the rhythm yourself.

lessons.title: Middle C area (left hand)
lessons.guide: Same ladder, left hand — lower octave (C3–G3). Pinky (finger 5) starts on C. Walk up, then back down.

tourSteps.text: Left hand: pinky (5) on C3, then fingers 4–3–2–1 on the next white keys up to G3.
Walk up C3 → G3. Orange keys show the left hand — same idea as the right-hand ladder.
Walk back down to C3. Your left hand mirrors what you learned on the right.
Take your time in Learn mode — each note waits for you. Ready? I'm ready → ▶

lessons.title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
lessons.guide: Your first full melody! Mostly stepwise notes in C major — sing the tune in your head as you play. Right hand only.

tourSteps.text: Same five-finger home: RH thumb on C. Most notes stay on C–G — no big jumps.
Press ▶ to hear the melody first. Notice how it climbs and comes back down.
Play each note when it hits the line. Learn mode waits — perfect for your first song!

lessons.title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
lessons.guide: A short, friendly melody — great for reading stepwise motion. Sing “Mary had a little lamb” as you play.

tourSteps.text: Right hand on C–G. This song hops between nearby notes — keep your hand relaxed.
Listen once with ▶. The pattern repeats — you'll hear it come back.
Ready? I'm ready → center ▶. Finger numbers show which key to press.

lessons.title: Ode to Joy (opening)
lessons.guide: Beethoven's famous theme — eight recognizable notes. Steady rhythm, mostly steps in the right hand.

tourSteps.text: You know this tune! Press ▶ and follow the rising shape of the melody.
RH five-finger position still works. Watch for E and G — fingers 3 and 5.
Take it slow in Learn mode. Each note waits until you play it correctly.
